summary.text: Michael Reilly is the Republican and Conservative Assembly Member for District 62 on Staten Island, running unopposed in 2026. A retired NYPD lieutenant and Army Reserve veteran, he led Community Education Council 31 before winning the seat in 2018, and he is the Ranking Minority Member of the Assembly's Cities Committee.

paragraphs.text: Reilly enlisted in the United States Army Reserve before joining the New York City Police Department, where he served 12 years and retired as a Lieutenant from Brooklyn's 90th Precinct.
He previously served as a volunteer member of the Staten Island YMCA's Board of Managers and coached the YMCA's youth baseball league.
In 2009 Reilly became a volunteer member of Community Education Council 31, focusing on accountability and transparency at NYC public schools.
He served as the Council's president from 2014 until his election to the Assembly in 2018 and became an advocate for traffic safety around school zones.

According to his campaign website, his work with the council included advocating for Drug Recognition Expert training for NYPD officers to address drugged driving, and a school safety plan that he says drew national attention.
Reilly won the open District 62 seat on November 6, 2018, defeating Reform Party candidate Glenn Yost in the general election; he succeeded Ronald Castorina and took office on January 1, 2019.
He was re-elected in 2020, 2022 and 2024 on the Republican and Conservative lines, and he is on the November 3, 2026 ballot unopposed.
His district includes the South Shore of Staten Island and parts of the Mid-Island.
Reilly is Ranking Minority Member of the Assembly Committee on Cities and a member of the Codes, Education, Governmental Employees, Higher Education, and Housing committees.

His official biography lists his priorities as education and transportation systems, school and community program funding, combatting the opioid crisis, and supporting law enforcement officers and public safety.
He lives in the Eltingville section of Staten Island with his wife and three children.
